author: Ethan Brooks
title: Padilla Sidesteps Governor Run Questions
text:

SACRAMENTO – Sen. Alex Padilla , 52, deflected questions Wednesday about a potential 2026 gubernatorial run, emphasizing his focus on a November special election concerning congressional redistricting.
U.S. Sen. Alex Padilla spoke at a political summit in Sacramento on Wednesday. Sen. Alex Padilla declined to rule out a 2026 gubernatorial bid. Padilla is focused on the November special election for congressional redistricting. He cited his long history of public service in California. Padilla Prioritizes Redistricting Battle Padilla stated, “I’m focused and I’d encourage everybody to focus on this Nov. 4 special election.” He argued the redistricting effort, championed by Gov.Gavin Newsom, counters Republican attempts to control Congress.
“So their only hope of staying in power beyond next November is to rig the system,” Padilla asserted, criticizing proposed budget cuts and tax breaks for billionaires. He believes such actions are unpopular and damaging.
Governor’s Race Speculation Mounts Padilla’s name has surfaced recently as a potential successor to Newsom, who is termed out. Polling indicates an unsettled field with manny undecided voters.
When asked about the appeal of the governor’s job, Padilla responded, “I love California, right? And I’ve had the privilege and the honor of serving in so many different capacities.”
A Career in California Politics Padilla began his political career in 1999, elected to the Los Angeles City Council at age 26. The Massachusetts Institute of Technology graduate lived with his parents in Pacoima at the time.
